items.title: Live: PM says move to next fuel security level is 'not imminent' following national cabinet meeting
items.description: Today's national cabinet meeting was "constructive", Anthony Albanese says, confirming that Australia remains at level 2 on its national fuel security plan.

items.title: Disability community scared and surprised by scale of planned NDIS overhaul
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler has defended the government's latest cost-cutting changes to the scheme in an interview with the ABC, amid an avalanche of participant concern.

items.title: 'Going out for coffee not a luxury': NDIS families grapple with planned cuts
items.description: An average cut of $7,000 to NDIS participant plans could hurt social supports, providing the "only interaction with the outside world" for some people with disability, advocates warn, as the minister concedes the savings will have a material impact on participant plans.

items.title: The proposed NDIS changes explained in five key points
items.description: Health Minister Mark Butler has unveiled sweeping cuts to the ballooning National Disability Insurance Scheme, aimed at cutting costs of the program down to $55 billion by the end of the decade.

items.title: We haven't seen budget decisions like this since Joe Hockey in 2014
items.description: As far as tough budget decisions go, we haven't seen anything on this scale since Joe Hockey's ill-fated 2014 effort.

items.title: James Valentine swapped microphones — and found a new audience who loved him
items.description: James Valentine started his career on the stage, but it was his time behind the microphone in the studio and an interactive style that came to define him.

items.title: E-7 Wedgetails are world leading, so why are they up for replacement?
items.description: Australia's fleet of world-leading surveillance aircraft is set to be replaced and analysts say the planes could be replaced by drones.

items.title: 'Bordering on bullying': Voss hits out at coverage of Hollands
items.description: Michael Voss has called out the media for the way it has covered Elijah Hollands's medical episode, saying the coverage of the 23-year-old "bordered on bullying".

items.title: Live: Iran attacks three cargo ships in strait, US Navy Secretary departs role
items.description: Iran has said it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the US naval blockade remains in place. Follow live.

items.title: Authors leave publisher after kids book cancelled for illustrator's comments
items.description: Writers including Evelyn Araluen and Randa Abdel-Fattah have left University of Queensland Press after the publisher axed publication of an Indigenous kids book over its illustrator's past 'anti-Semitic' comments.

items.title: Actor suing Rebel Wilson agrees bath incident was 'strange and bizarre'
items.description: A young actor suing Rebel Wilson for defamation has given details in court about an incident at Bondi Beach, which she claims the Hollywood star has since mischaracterised.

items.title: Kingpin's private phone calls break open Mongols' 'culture of silence'
items.description: Detectives say bikies are recruiting inside Northern Territory prisons, as a kingpin's tapped private phone calls offer a rare glimpse into the underground world of outlaw motorcycle gangs.

items.title: Live: 'Like a slasher movie' as major ASX stock crashes
items.description: Major healthcare stock Cochlear crashed yesterday. Buyers have not moved in today. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Small WA town takes centre stage for Netflix series filming
items.description: There is a buzz about town in a small community north of Perth as filming begins for a new Netflix series.

items.title: This man plays the last post to a different fallen Anzac every day
items.description: Adam Farquharson feels the honour of Anzac Day every day as he plays to a different veteran's grave.

items.title: Stump that created hole in footpath becomes neighbourhood attraction
items.description: Adelaide residents have decorated a large tree stump and then the hole it left in a footpath to highlight the local council's delay in removing it.

items.title: Removing plastic from our food chain yields quick results, researchers say
items.description: Perth researchers find levels of plastic chemicals in the body can be reduced within a week by avoiding plastic food packaging and kitchen utensils.

items.title: Leading Trump envoy suggests FIFA replace Iran with Italy at World Cup
items.description: As the US president feuds with Pope Leo, one of his top envoys suggests giving Italy a World Cup spot could mend fences.

items.title: Women on mission to preserve history of town's soldier settlers
items.description: Anzac Day holds meaning for every Australian, but for Marie Carman and Lorelei King, it is another reminder of their deeply personal mission to uncover the forgotten stories of the soldiers who helped build their town.

items.title: Police officer given 'golden pass' on rape allegations, victim says
items.description: When Tasmania Police misidentified Laura as a family violence perpetrator, she had no idea she'd have to fight for them to hold her abuser — a serving officer — to account. Now, she's fighting for change.

items.title: New AI threat looms but Australian firms don't have access needed to prepare
items.description: Local banks, power providers and infrastructure firms do not have access to test their systems against a powerful new AI cybersecurity risk, Anthropic's Mythos, which has not been made public.

items.title: Pacific leaders 'totally blindsided' by declaration of fuel emergency
items.description: Confusion and some frustration remains after a key Pacific leader announced an emergency declaration had been agreed to over fuel, despite other leaders not knowing about it.

items.title: 'Not a great look': Piastri weighs in on Verstappen's F1 frustrations
items.description: Australian star Oscar Piastri speaks as Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen looks increasingly likely to walk away from the sport.

items.title: Farmers say an easy solution to the mouse plague has been rejected
items.description: Farmers are pushing for stronger bait approval as mice numbers soar out of control in Western Australia, but stronger poisons are being rejected by the national chemical regulator.

items.title: No more green bin pick-ups for some residents amid fuel uncertainty
items.description: The Upper Lachlan Shire Council says it cannot afford to be caught off-guard if a diesel shipment does not arrive, and must reserve fuel for essential services like road grading or red bin collections.
